title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Communications
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response processes, a set of canonical runbooks, postmortem guidance, rotation policies, game day practices, and templates for status page & customer communications. It is intended to be the operational reference for engineers, SREs, support, and customer success during production incidents.

Scope
- Production services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private control plane)
- Incident severities: Sev0 (service down), Sev1 (degraded, major customer impact), Sev2 (partial degradation), Sev3 (minor/operational)
- Applies to Redwood staff with on-call responsibilities and service owners

Key Definitions
- Incident Commander (IC): Single decision-maker for the overall incident until delegation/hand-off. Responsible for triage, coordination, customer updates, and declaring incident end.
- Primary on-call: First responder for paging alerts; owns initial triage.
- Secondary on-call: Escalation target if primary unavailable or incident requires multiple responders.
- Subject Matter Expert (SME): Dev/infra owner with deep knowledge of the impacted service.
- War Room: Slack channel + Zoom (if needed) for coordination.

Severity Matrix and SLAs
- Sev0: "API unavailable for >90% of customers" — Pager triggered, immediate paging to primary + ops lead, target MTTR <30m.
- Sev1: "Critical degraded latency or errors impacting >20% of requests/customers" — Pager + on-call + SMEs, target MTTR <2h.
- Sev2: "Localized degradation or non-critical errors" — Alert to on-call, target MTTR <24h.
- Sev3: "Minor issue, informational" — Ticket, handle in normal workflow.

Alerting & Paging Policy
1. Alert thresholds are configured in PagerDuty and routed by service and severity.
2. Page primary on-call for Sev0/Sev1 alerts. If no ack in 3 minutes, escalate to secondary.
3. For repeated alerts (>3 similar alerts in 10m) auto-open incident in Incident Manager and notify IC.
4. Use structured alert messages: service | region | metric | value | runbook_link

Incident Lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Triage (first 0–10 minutes)
   - Primary on-call acknowledges pager and posts initial message in #ops-incidents (template below).
   - Determine scope: affected services, regions, customer impact, whether this is a known ongoing event.
   - Run quick health checks and consult the relevant runbook.
2. Declare & Staff (10–30 minutes)
   - If incident meets Sev1/Sev0 criteria, IC is assigned (either primary or senior on-call).
   - Create war room Slack channel and Zoom if needed (IC creates #incident-<short-id>).
   - Notify product, support, and communications owners.
3. Mitigate (30–90 minutes)
   - Perform mitigation actions from runbook (rollback, traffic diversion, restart nodes, scale up capacity, apply hotfix).
   - Coordinate with infra to increase capacity or route traffic to healthy regions.
   - Enable temporary customer-visible mitigations (rate limits, degraded mode) if available and approved.
4. Communicate (ongoing)
   - Internal updates: every 15–30 minutes for Sev0/Sev1 until stable.
   - External updates: status.redwood.ai + customer email/CS updates at 30–60 minute cadence for Sev0/Sev1 (templates below).
5. Recovery & Verification
   - Confirm service health metrics (latency, error rate, throughput) have returned to baseline for a minimum of 15 minutes.
   - Run synthetic checks and sample customer requests to validate correctness.
6. Declare End & Post-incident (within 24h)
   - IC declares incident resolved in war room channel and Status Page.
   - Create postmortem ticket and assign owner. Postmortem draft due within 72 hours; final published postmortem due within 7 days.

Canonical Runbooks (what to include)
Each runbook must be a standalone doc with the following top-level sections:
- Purpose & scope
- Observable symptoms and alert signatures
- Quick triage checklist (commands, dashboards, logs)
- Mitigation steps (ordered, safe to execute first, high-risk steps flagged)
- Rollback / recovery steps
- Post-incident actions & required follow-ups
- Owners and escalation list
- Links to related runbooks / ADRs / dashboards

Example Runbook: API Gateway 5xx Surge
- Symptoms: 5xx rate > 2% for 5 min and p50 latency > 800ms
- Quick checks:
  - kubectl -n api get pods | grep gateway
  - curl -sv https://api.redwood.ai/health
  - Grafana dashboard: API Gateway - Errors
- Mitigations (ordered):
  1. Drain unhealthy pods from load balancer (low risk)
  2. Increase replicas from 3 -> 6 (if autoscaler limited)
  3. Disable non-essential background jobs (if suspected cause)
  4. Roll back recent deployment (if deployment within 30m and correlated)
  5. If memory leak suspected, restart pods one-by-one with priority scheduling
- Safety notes: Rolling restarts may briefly increase error rate; schedule during quiet minutes unless Sev0.

Runbook Maintenance
- Every runbook must have an owner and a last-tested date.
- Owners must re-run the runbook on staging quarterly and update the last-tested field.
- Runbooks with no updates or tests for 12 months are flagged for review.

Postmortem Process & Template
Timeline:
- Within 24h: Create postmortem issue with initial facts, timeline and ownership.
- Draft due within 72h.
- Review meeting scheduled within 7 days with stakeholders.
- Final publish within 7 days with action items and owners.
Postmortem required fields (flat list):
- Title
- Incident ID and severity
- Summary (one-paragraph customer-friendly)
- Impact (customers affected, duration, SLO breaches)
- Timeline (timestamped events)
- Root cause analysis (what happened and why)
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations)
- Preventive actions (longer-term engineering work)
- Action owner and due date for each action
- Lessons learned
- Verification plan for each preventive action

Blamelessness & Culture
- Postmortems are blameless; focus on systems and process improvements.
- Celebrate good responses and identify what helped.

On-call Rotations & Handoffs
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary rotations (default), 1 week secondary rotations at team discretion.
- Coverage: 24/7 for production-critical services.
- Handoff procedure:
  1. Outgoing on-call posts a Handoff message in #team-oncall with: current incidents, outstanding action items, scheduled maintenance, and known flaky alerts.
  2. Incoming on-call acknowledges and confirms understanding.
  3. For longer shifts (>48h) or international handovers, include a short 10–15 minute sync.
- Backup policy: If on-call is unavailable for the shift, they must arrange a documented swap at least 24 hours prior.

Escalation Matrix
- Primary on-call -> Secondary on-call (3 min) -> Team lead (10 min) -> Eng manager (20 min) -> Director on-call (escalated for Sev0 after 30m)
- For security incidents, notify security@redwood.ai immediately and follow security incident runbook.

Game Days (regular exercises)
Purpose: Validate runbooks, telemetry, paging, and cross-team coordination.
Cadence: Quarterly per major product pillar, additional milestone game days for major releases.
Typical agenda:
1. Pre-game checklist: select target service, restore point, and create test customers.
2. Inject fault (simulated latency, node termination, high error rate).
3. Run full incident lifecycle; time the MTTR and collect metrics.
4. Debrief (30–60m) with facilitators and capture action items.
5. Update runbooks and monitor for regression with a follow-up task.
Success metrics: mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), accuracy of communications, runbook execution completeness.

Status Page & Customer Communications Templates
- Principle: Be proactive, transparent, timely, consistent. Use customer-friendly language that avoids jargon.
- Status Page Components: short summary, impact, affected services, region, incident start time, next update ETA, mitigation in progress, resolved time.

Status Page Example (short message)
Title: Partial Outage — Hosted API (US-West)\Summary: We are experiencing increased error rates for API requests in US-West. Engineers are investigating and mitigation is in progress.\Impact: Customers in US-West may see 5xx errors and increased latency; other regions not affected.\Start Time: 2026-02-10T09:22:00Z\Next Update: in 30 minutes\\n

Customer Email Template (initial)\Subject: Incident: API interruptions in US-West — Engineers investigating\Hi <CustomerName>,\We’re reaching out to let you know that some API requests to our US‑West region are returning errors. Our engineers are investigating and we’ve put mitigations in place to reduce customer impact. We’ll send updates every 30–60 minutes until this is resolved.\If you have a critical workflow impacted, reply to this email or contact your CS rep directly at cs@redwood.ai.\Sincerely,\Redwood Inference Operations

Customer Email Template (follow-up / resolution)\Subject: Incident resolved: API interruptions in US-West\Hi <CustomerName>,\The issue affecting the US‑West API has been resolved at 10:14 UTC. We saw elevated errors between 09:22–10:14 UTC; services have returned to expected behavior and monitored metrics are stable.\Impact: Brief summary of customers or SLOs impacted.\Root cause summary: Short blameless explanation (e.g., deployment rollback required due to edge case in gateway).\Next steps: Relevant mitigations, planned follow-ups, and link to postmortem when published.\Thank you for your patience — contact cs@redwood.ai for any follow up.\\n

Internal Incident Announcement (Slack template)\Channel: #ops-incidents\Message: @channel — Incident [INC-<id>] declared Sev1 for API Gateway (US-West). IC: <name>. Brief: Increased 5xx and latency. War room: #incident-<id>. Initial triage in progress. Customer impact: yes.\\n

Communications Roles & Ownership\- IC: approves content before publishing to status page\- Communications lead (usually TA/PR or CS lead): drafts customer-facing messages and coordinates approvals\- Support: posts templated CS notes to impacted customers and updates ticketing systems

Post-incident Follow-up & Tracking\- Action items from postmortem must have a clear owner, due date, and verification criteria.\- Track all actions in the engineering backlog with the label "incident-action".\- SRE leadership reviews outstanding incident actions monthly.

Appendices\A. Quick links (examples)\- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.example.com/services/redwood\- Status Page: https://status.redwood.ai\- Incident Manager / Postmortem template: /confluence/eng-sre/postmortem-template\- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks-index
\B. Contact list (roles)\- On-call rotation manager: rotations@redwood.ai\- Major incident pager: +1-555-0100 (internal only)\- Security: security@redwood.ai

Change Log\- 2025-11-12: Initial published playbook (Priya Natarajan).\- 2026-02-10: Updated runbook testing cadence, tightened paging escalation (reviewers: Evan Brooks, Maya Thompson).

If anything in this playbook is unclear, contact the on-call rotation manager or open an RFC in /confluence/eng-sre for process changes.
